title: Phyllis Lambert
body: Phyllis Barbara Lambert is a Canadianphilanthropist and member of the Bronfman family. On 17 May 1949, in Montreal, she married Jean Lambert, a French-Germaneconomic consultant and the only son of Adolphe Lambert of Elmhurst, Queens, New York.The couple divorced in 1954. Lambert moved to New York City in 1954 and became involved in architecture; she graduated from the Illinois Institute of Technology in 1963. In the 1960s, she designed the Saidye Bronfman Centre in Montreal, named after her mother. As Director of Planning for the Seagram Building, she was influential in bringing Ludwig Mies van der Rohe onto the project, also recommending him for the Toronto-Dominion Centre design.
